sources_considered.why: Primary evidence of external full-model hosting and workload-dependent commercial pricing.
Primary report of an independent inference-system reproduction, including a cost estimate and limitations.
Search identified a reproduction project announcement; an announced plan alone does not establish completed reproduction or serving economics.
Search identified later B200 measurements. They do not directly establish the economics of the original pricing under early-2025 deployment conditions.

evidence_items.locator: Section: Running DeepSeek-R1 on Together Serverless offers
evidence_items.explanation: The announcement establishes external hosting of full R1. Its cluster prices depend on a specified input/output mix and contract commitments, so they are not directly equivalent to DeepSeek's separate token prices.

evidence_items.locator: Section: Highlight, second bullet; introduction and Limitations and Future Work
evidence_items.explanation: This establishes recreation of relevant inference methods and external V3 deployment. The authors estimate $0.20 per million output tokens, but identify latency and sequence-length limitations; this favors the claim without settling both full models' commercial economics.

metric_scope.company: SGLang Team / Atlas Cloud deployment of DeepSeek-V3

unresolved_gaps: The strongest reproduction measures V3 under a limited workload, rather than matching both V3 and R1 commercial serving costs.
The sources do not reconcile all relevant operating costs with the original separate input and output prices.
Recreation of inference methods does not establish recreation of all training methods, if that broader condition was intended.
